newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf to move corporate office to Denver.
newsitem.headline: Gulf to move corporate office to Denver.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, the Canadian oil and gas producer that last year came under the control of Texan J.P. Bryan, said on Wednesday it planned to move its corporate office to Denver from Calgary.

Gulf Canada, which underwent a major corporate restructuring starting in January 1995, said the move would provide it with better access to primary capital markets and better exposure to investment and acquisition opportunities.
The company made the announcement in a statement reporting that it posted third-quarter earnings per share of nil, compared to a year earlier loss of C$0.02.
Under the plan, 20 of Gulf Canada's 25 corporate staff would move to Denver, including chief executive Bryan.
The company said it would remain a Canadian firm subject to the country's regulatory and reporting requirements and that all North American operations would be run from Calgary.
Gulf Canada, which also operates in the United States and Indonesia, said the move was part of its plan to become a major international oil and gas company.
